 Middleware 
 
 runs for every request before path operation every response before returned for cross - cutting concerns : timing logging compression host checks CORS, request IDs. 
 
 Writing HTTP middleware 
 
 Decorate async function with @ app. middleware ( " http " ) docs_src tutorial001_py310 
 
```python
import time

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request

app = FastAPI()


@app.middleware("http")
async def add_process_time_header(request: Request, call_next):
    start_time = time.perf_counter()
    response = await call_next(request)
    process_time = time.perf_counter() - start_time
    response.headers["X-Process-Time"] = str(process_time)
    return response
```
 
 function receives 
 
 request Request 
 call_next function passes request to rest app inner middleware path operation returns response. 
 
 run code before call_next inspect modify request short - circuit returning response after modify response )

 headers use X - prefix. browser JS cross - origin CORS expose_headers CORS

 Adding ASGI middleware classes 
 
 ASGI middleware works doesn't be written for FastAPI ASGI middlewares classes taking app as first argument Third - party docs show : 
 
```python
from unicorn import UnicornMiddleware

app = SomeASGIApp()
new_app = UnicornMiddleware(app, some_config="rainbow")
```
 
FastAPI use add_middleware ( ) instead keeps FastAPI ' s exception handling middleware stack intact : 
 
```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from unicorn import UnicornMiddleware

app = FastAPI()

app.add_middleware(UnicornMiddleware, some_config="rainbow")
```
 
 pass middleware = [ Middleware (... ) ] to FastAPI (... ). 
 
 Execution order 
 
 Each added middleware wraps app built last one added outermost 
 
```python
app.add_middleware(MiddlewareA)
app.add_middleware(MiddlewareB)
```
 
 - Request : MiddlewareB → MiddlewareA → route 
 - Response : route → MiddlewareA → MiddlewareB 
 
 applies to @ app. middleware ( add_middleware ( middleware sits outside FastAPI ' s exception handlers sees responses ( 404, 422 custom handlers ) inside ServerErrorMiddleware turns unhandled exceptions into 500 responses How FastAPI Handles a Request ] internals request - handling internals full stack 
 
 Built - in middleware 
 
 FastAPI re - exports common Starlette middleware in fastapi. middleware. 
 
 HTTPSRedirectMiddleware 
 
 Redirects every http request to https : 
 
```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.httpsredirect import HTTPSRedirectMiddleware

app = FastAPI()

app.add_middleware(HTTPSRedirectMiddleware)
```
 
 TLS termination proxy forwarded headers trusted app request http redirect in loop proxy handles redirect HTTPS and Cloud ] deployment / https - cloud md ). 
 
 TrustedHostMiddleware 
 
 Rejects requests Host header isn't protects against HTTP Host header attacks : 
 
```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.trustedhost import TrustedHostMiddleware

app = FastAPI()

app.add_middleware(
    TrustedHostMiddleware, allowed_hosts=["example.com", "*.example.com"]
)
```
 
 - allowed_hosts domain names hostnames wildcards example. com match subdomains. omitting middleware allows 
 - www_redirect redirect non - www requests to www. version allowed host ( default True ) 
 
Invalid hosts get 400 response 
 
 GZipMiddleware 
 
 Compresses responses for clients gzip Accept - Encoding : 
 
```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.gzip import GZipMiddleware

app = FastAPI()

app.add_middleware(GZipMiddleware, minimum_size=1000, compresslevel=5)
```
 
 - minimum_size don't compress responses smaller bytes default 500 ) 
 - compresslevel 1 ( fast, larger ) to 9 ( slow, smaller ) default 9
